objective: To implement an automated electrical control system for a banquet hall that manages lights, fans, and ACs based on real-time occupancy detection, eliminating manual intervention after initial setup. The system aims to achieve significant energy savings by ensuring appliances operate only when zones are occupied while maintaining guest comfort during events. Staff will monitor system status through accessible dashboards but will not need to manually control appliances during normal operations.

architecture: The system follows a real-time monitoring and control architecture with three main layers: sensor input, control logic, and appliance actuation. Motion sensors installed in each banquet hall zone continuously detect occupancy and send detection events via Zigbee/ZWave protocol to a central gateway controller. The gateway forwards these events to the core application server running on-premises, which processes occupancy patterns using predefined rules (e.g., occupancy threshold of 1+ person triggers appliance activation). The server then sends control commands via GPIO or relay modules to physical switches controlling lights, fans, and ACs in each zone. All detection events and appliance state changes are logged to the local PostgreSQL database. The web dashboard running on Nginx serves real-time status updates to staff mobile devices and wall-mounted displays via WebSocket connections, showing current occupancy status, appliance states, and system health metrics. Manual override commands from staff flow back through the same path in reverse: dashboard → API → control logic → relay modules.

techStack.rationale: Provides responsive, installable dashboard accessible on both mobile devices and wall-mounted screens without native app development overhead.
Lightweight, high-performance framework ideal for real-time event processing with built-in WebSocket support for dashboard updates.
Reliable ACID-compliant RDBMS for storing event logs and system configuration with strong data integrity for operational tracking.

techStack.choice: On-premises Raspberry Pi 4 cluster + Ubuntu Server
techStack.rationale: Low-cost, energy-efficient local hosting ensures minimal latency for real-time control and avoids cloud dependency for critical automation.
Simple yet secure access control for dashboard without complex SSO requirements suitable for internal staff use only.

techStack.choice: Xiaomi Mi Human Body Motion Sensor 2 (Zigbee)
techStack.rationale: Cost-effective, reliable Zigbee sensors with good detection range and battery life, compatible with local gateway control.
Reliable smart relays that can interface with existing electrical switches via GPIO, allowing remote control of non-smart appliances.
Open-source Zigbee gateway solution that bridges sensor data to the application server via MQTT/HTTP protocols.
Automated testing and deployment pipeline for application updates while maintaining simple on-premises deployment workflow.

userFlow: System administrator logs into configuration dashboard using staff credentials
Administrator defines banquet hall zones on interactive floor plan map
Administrator assigns motion sensors to each zone by scanning Zigbee device IDs
Administrator configures appliance mapping: which lights, fans, and ACs correspond to each zone
Administrator sets occupancy rules: minimum occupancy count (default 1) and timeout delay before turning off appliances after zone empties
Administrator saves configuration and activates automated mode
System begins monitoring: motion sensors detect occupancy in zones
When occupancy detected in zone, system automatically turns on assigned lights, then fans, then ACs with staggered delay
When zone empties and timeout period elapses, system turns off appliances in reverse order
Staff member views real-time dashboard showing zone occupancy status (green/red indicators)
Staff member sees appliance state icons (on/off) for each zone
Staff member can manually override any zone by clicking appliance toggle buttons
Staff member views historical logs showing motion events and energy usage patterns
Maintenance staff receives email alerts if any sensor goes offline for extended period

dataModel.description: Defined physical area within banquet hall with boundaries for occupancy detection and appliance control
Physical motion detection device installed in specific zone, reporting occupancy events
Electrical device (light, fan, AC) controlled by relay module, mapped to specific zone
Log entry for each motion detection (occupied/empty) from sensors with timestamp
Audit trail of every appliance state change (on/off), whether automated or manual override
Rule configuration per zone controlling automation behavior and timing parameters
Staff members with dashboard access, roles determine override permissions

pageBehavior.description: Simple username/password form with JWT token generation; redirects to dashboard on successful authentication; includes 'forgot password' link for admin reset.

Interactive floor plan map of banquet hall where admin can draw polygons to define zones; drag-and-drop sensor icons onto zones; form to name zones and set basic parameters; save button triggers configuration validation.

Grid view showing all appliances (lights, fans, ACs) with dropdown to assign each to a zone; includes relay module ID and GPIO pin configuration fields; test button sends momentary on/off signal to verify control.

Per-zone cards with sliders for occupancy threshold (default 1), turn-on delay (0.60 seconds), turn-off delay (5-30 minutes), and appliance stagger delay (lights immediate, fans 30s delay, ACs 60s delay); toggle switch for auto/manual mode per zone.

Primary staff view: color-coded zone indicators (green=occupied, red=empty); appliance status icons with on/off labels; manual override toggle buttons per appliance; real-time occupancy count per zone; system health status bar.
Filterable table showing occupancy events and appliance state changes by date range, zone, or appliance type; export to CSV functionality; visual timeline showing occupancy patterns throughout day.
Shows sensor battery levels, relay connectivity status, network latency metrics; alert history panel; manual sensor test buttons; system restart controls (admin only).
Full-screen simplified version of monitoring dashboard optimized for touch interaction; auto-refreshing every 10 seconds; emergency manual override large buttons with confirmation dialogs.

securityDesign: JWT authentication with 24-hour expiration for all dashboard API access
Role-based access control: staff can only view and override, admin can configure settings
All sensor data and control commands transmitted over local VLAN isolated from guest WiFi
HTTPS enforced for all web dashboard communications with self-signed certificates for local network
Password hashing using bcrypt with minimum 12-character requirement for staff accounts
Automatic session timeout after 30 minutes of dashboard inactivity
Rate limiting on control API endpoints to prevent rapid toggling attacks
Physical security: relay control modules in locked electrical cabinet with tamper detection
Audit logging of all manual overrides with staff user ID and timestamp
No storage of personal identifiable information - only operational event data
Regular security patches applied via automated Docker container updates
deploymentAndOperations: Three environments: Development (Docker containers on engineer laptops), Staging (identical hardware setup in test area), Production (actual banquet hall installation)
CI/CD pipeline: GitHub Actions runs unit tests on push, builds Docker images, deploys to staging automatically, requires manual approval for production deployment
Production monitoring: Prometheus metrics collection for system uptime, sensor connectivity, response latency; Grafana dashboard for real-time visualization
Alerting: Email notifications to maintenance staff for sensor failures, relay disconnections, or system downtime exceeding 5 minutes
Backup strategy: Daily automated PostgreSQL backups to external NAS with 30-day retention; configuration backups before every deployment
Disaster recovery: Cold standby Raspberry Pi with pre-loaded Docker images ready for swap if primary hardware fails
Rollback procedure: Versioned Docker images allow immediate rollback to previous working version via single command
Maintenance window: Scheduled weekly on Tuesday mornings 2-4 AM for updates when hall is unoccupied
Power resilience: UPS backup for control server and gateway ensuring 2-hour operation during power outages
Documentation: Runbooks for common troubleshooting scenarios accessible to non-technical staff via internal wiki

timeline.description: Purchase motion sensors, relay modules, Raspberry Pi hardware; conduct site survey to map zones, electrical points, and network infrastructure; create detailed floor plan.
Build FastAPI backend with event processing logic, database schema, Zigbee gateway integration, and relay control modules; implement basic WebSocket dashboard.
Develop React PWA with zone configuration interface, real-time monitoring views, and manual override controls; optimize for mobile and wall displays.
Physical installation of sensors and relay modules; integration testing of full control loop from motion detection to appliance actuation; load testing with simulated occupancy patterns.
Implement JWT auth, role-based access, network isolation, audit logging; conduct security review of control pathways and data storage.
Set up identical staging environment in test area; train staff on configuration and monitoring; gather feedback and refine UI/UX.
Install in actual banquet hall during off-hours; migrate configuration; conduct formal training sessions for all staff members; create operational documentation.
24/7 monitoring of first events; fine-tune delay parameters based on actual usage patterns; address any edge cases discovered in production.

assumptions: Existing electrical wiring and switches can support relay module integration without major rewiring
Banquet hall has stable WiFi network covering all zones for sensor gateway connectivity
Staff have access to smartphones or tablets for mobile dashboard access
Wall-mounted display locations have power and network connectivity
Motion sensors will be installed at optimal heights and locations for accurate occupancy detection
Electrical loads (lights, fans, ACs) are within relay module specifications
No existing building automation system conflicts with this new installation
Staff will undergo basic training on dashboard usage and manual override procedures
Power backup (UPS) will be provisioned for critical control components
Maintenance staff can perform basic troubleshooting like restarting services

Approval process for physical modifications to electrical panels
Emergency override procedures coordination with existing hall safety protocols
